column2: Al-Nawawī's Forty Hadiths, with Ibn Rajab's addition to them, and with the commentary al-Sharḥ al-Mūjaz al-Mufīd (The Concise, Beneficial Commentary) (ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Muḥsin)
Category: Books of the Sunnah
Book: Al-Nawawī's Forty Hadiths, with Ibn Rajab's addition to them, and with the commentary al-Sharḥ al-Mūjaz al-Mufīd
Author: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Muḥsin
Publisher: The Islamic University, Madīnah
Edition: Third, 1404 AH / 1984 CE
Number of pages: 94
[The book's pagination matches the printed edition]
Date of publication on al-Shāmilah: 8 Dhū al-Ḥijjah 1431 AH
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Introduction
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the noble Prophet, and upon his family, his Companions and the Successors.
To proceed:

Since al-Nawawī's Forty Hadiths have several commentaries and annotations, some of which do not adequately cover the important meanings and some of which are lengthy, I decided to write a concise commentary following the modern method of teaching, together with the eight hadiths that Ibn Rajab added.
I have set out first the text of the hadith,
then its vocabulary, then its benefits,
then the concise commentary on the hadith, and then whatever beneficial verses of poetry are readily available on the meaning of the hadith.
I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Mighty Throne, Lord of the worlds, to make this work of mine fruitful and beneficial, both now and later.
He is All-Hearing, Near and Responsive. May Allah send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad and upon his family and Companions. The author:
ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Muḥsin
Teacher at the Islamic University, Madīnah
Preface
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Commendation:
All praise is due to Allah alone, and blessings and peace be upon the one after whom there is no prophet.
To proceed:

I have read this great commentary in which our brother, His Eminence Shaykh ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Muḥsin, teacher at the Islamic University in the city of the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him), explained al-Nawawī's Forty Hadiths together with the eight that the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab added.

He has been beneficial and excellent in explaining their wording in a way suited to the level of students of knowledge in schools and elsewhere, and he has eased their path to understanding them, for he has arranged it as follows:
(1) Explaining their vocabulary.
(2) Setting out the benefits drawn from each of them.
(3) The overall meaning of each hadith.
(4) Mentioning some verses of poetry in keeping with each hadith.
Students of Prophetic knowledge should therefore hasten to acquire it and read it.
I ask Allah, the Most High, the All-Powerful, to benefit with this concise commentary whoever reads it or copies it, and to reward its compiler with the best reward. Āmīn.
The one who hopes for his Lord's pardon,
Ḥammād ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī
Teacher at the Islamic University, Madīnah

May Allah send blessings upon our master Muḥammad as many times as those who remember make mention of him, and upon all his family and Companions. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Āmīn.
